title: Caspian languages - Wikipedia
text: The Caspian languages are a key branch of North-Western Iranian languages spoken in Iran and parts of the Azerbaijan Republic, south and west of the Caspian Sea. They are also unique in sharing some typological features with the Kartvelian languages.

title: Takestani Language (TKS) – L1 & L2 Speakers... | Ethnologue Free
text: Takestani is an endangered indigenous language of Iran. It belongs to the Indo-European language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by adults only.
